transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because after I do it, after I eat like that, I end up sitting there looking at the empty containers and I just feel disgusted with myself. It makes me feel like I’m not the steady, in-control man I’ve always tried to be.
After you eat like that, do you ever make yourself vomit or do something else to try to compensate for the food you've eaten?
I don’t know. I mean, I haven’t really thought of it that way. Afterward I usually just feel bad and kind of sit with it. I’m not sure what would count as “compensating,” I guess.
Do you find yourself eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most people would eat during a similar period under similar circumstances?

Yes. Some evenings I’ll tell myself I’m just having one bowl of pozole, but then I end up going through the whole pot. And then maybe a couple tamales, chips, whatever leftovers are around. It’s definitely more than a normal meal—more like I’m feeding a whole crew, except it’s just me.
When you're eating this large amount of food, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yes. Once I start, it’s like the discipline I have when I’m working, when I’m on the road, just shuts off. I’ll be telling myself, Magin, put the fork down, that’s enough, but my hand still goes back for more. It feels like I’m not really in control in that moment.
Do you have these episodes of binge eating regularly, like several times a week, even if you don’t do anything to compensate afterward?

Yes. Since I’ve been home with my back injury, it’s been happening several nights most weeks. I honestly can’t think of a week in the last three months where I didn’t have at least one of those nights.
Do these episodes of binge eating bother you a lot or cause you significant distress?

Yes, it bothers me a lot. Afterward I’ll just sit there and look at all the empty containers, and I feel disgusted with myself. It’s like… that’s not the steady, in-control man I’ve always tried to be.
Have these binge eating episodes caused you a lot of problems in your daily life, like interfering with work, relationships, or how you see yourself?

Yes. I’ve started avoiding check-in calls from the drivers I’m supposed to be mentoring. I feel ashamed, like they’ll hear in my voice how far off my routine I’ve gotten. It’s affecting how I see myself, and I don’t like that.
